topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's core themes, relates them to earlier course concepts, and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and transient epigenetic changes confer selective fitness advantages to drive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and the cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies and tumorigenesis, evaluating evidence for cancer stem cells and cells of origin in leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, chronic inflammation, and stromal support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory signals, environmental promoters, and supportive stromal cells cooperate with mutations to permit neoplastic outgrowth and progression.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys the sequencing, spatial profiling, and computational techniques used to map clonal evolution and cellular interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Integrative synthesis of multifactorial cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic mutations, cell-of-origin properties, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental conditions collectively orchestrate cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic brings the session to a close and previews the subsequent lecture on cancer therapy.
